minutes.headline: ZBA voted to uphold the building inspector: the first 20 feet of the 72 Peninsula Drive fence must come down to 36 inches.
minutes.summary: The Zoning Board of Appeals heard an appeal by the owners of 72 Peninsula Drive against the building inspector's order to reduce two street-side fence panels to 36 inches. Neighbors at 76 Peninsula Drive opposed the appeal and raised the rest of the fence as well. The board voted to uphold the inspector's decision and told the owners to work with him on compliance.

Rebuttal on response timing, survey stake, backing out, and fence panel heights.

what_happened.line: The Zoning Board of Appeals voted to uphold the building commissioner's decision that the first 20 feet of fence at 72 Peninsula Drive be reduced to 36 inches.
The owners were told to work with the building inspector on bringing the fence into conformance; the captions record a round of ayes but no count.
The owners had asked that the fence be accepted as is, saying it replaced arborvitae, sits on their property, and that they did not know of the 20-foot rule.
Neighbors at 76 Peninsula Drive opposed the appeal, questioned the changed determination and notice, and raised the rest of the fence, including two lakeside panels.
The written decision is to be filed with the town clerk within 14 days, and an appeal to Superior Court may be made within 20 days of filing.

why_it_matters: For residents with a fence near a street, this shows the board applying the 20-foot street-side height limit as the building inspector read it, even where the owner says they did not know of the rule.
The hearing concerned one property and no town spending, but the decision sets a local example of how fence height and setback complaints between neighbors get resolved.
watch_next: Written decision due with the town clerk within 14 days of the vote.
Window to appeal to Superior Court runs 20 days from the filing of the decision.
